answer: An agent market handling tasks such as pricing opal, mapping a canyon, or tracking a dune can require each identity to lock a refundable bond. Jobs are assigned in proportion to bonded funds, so splitting one deposit across a thousand identities gives no extra share of work. To gain influence, an attacker must lock up more capital; if an agent submits conflicting signed results for the same job, a verifiable fraud proof triggers forfeiture of its bond.
